apis.name: validateAnimationAsset
apis.signature: validateAnimationAsset(unknown) -> Array<{ code: string; path: string; message: string }>
constraints: Pure validation of flamo.animation-asset version 1: pixel-local size/source crop, parent bones, invertible bind poses, skin mesh weights, triangle indices and named poses. Empty issues means data validation only, not rendered or visual acceptance.
At most 256 bones, 4096 vertices and 8192 triangles per mesh; 1..4 known weights per vertex must sum to 1. Anatomy and missing pixels are never inferred.

apis.name: AnimationSurface
apis.signature: surface.clear(); draw(source, x?, y?, width?, height?); drawMesh(source, vertices, triangles); applyMatte(source, 'alpha' | 'luminance'); commit() -> number; dispose()
constraints: Create through app.createAnimationSurface with a unique id and fixed integer dimensions 1..2048. Reuse the surface; bind its id as the assetId of a native Scene IMAGE.
Vertices contain x/y in surface pixels and u/v in source pixels. Matte must already align to the same coordinates and decoded time. Explicit alpha or luminance masking is not automatic segmentation.
commit uploads a new image revision. dispose clears visibility and invalidates further writes; stable texture allocation is reclaimed with the owning pool. Do not resize or reuse disposed ids.

apis.name: videoRegistry.seekFrame
apis.signature: videoRegistry.seekFrame(id, timeMs, { timeoutMs?, signal?, maxFrameErrorMs? }?) -> Promise<VideoFrameReceipt>
constraints: Use the owning Flamo resource pool videoRegistry and registered media. Read the decoded-time receipt, validate the allowed deviation, and snapshot pixels during timeline prepare; a live video element is not a stable prepared frame.

Caller coordinates same-time color/matte seeks and serializes/coalesces requests for each media source. Abort/obsolete frames must not update the visible scene. This does not synthesize video, speech or alignment.

apis.name: app.createAnimationSurface
constraints: Small CPU Canvas2D mesh/matte surface, fixed dimensions 1..2048. Pool budget is 16M dynamic pixels and 64 ids, retained until pool destruction. Reuse surfaces across frames. Append a Scene IMAGE with assetId equal to surface.id; no DOM renderer overlay.
clear/draw/drawMesh/applyMatte modify staging pixels; commit advances the native texture revision. UV coordinates are source pixels; vertex positions are surface pixels.

Unique image ids belong to the resource pool. Dispose clears visibility and rejects further commits; stable GPU allocation is reclaimed when the owning pool is destroyed. Do not resize or reuse disposed ids.

apis.name: Skeleton2D
apis.signature: new Skeleton2D(asset); setPose(localPose); deform(mesh); joint(id); boneTransform(id)
constraints: Versioned flamo.animation-asset v1 uses local pixel bind transforms, degrees and normalized per-vertex weights. Unknown parents, cycles, zero scales and invalid triangles are rejected.
setPose is absolute local pose with omitted fields retaining bind values. Skinning applies posedWorld times inverseBind. Anatomy and behavior belong to the project; Runtime does not infer them.

setMixedPose mixes partial clips against this skeleton's bind transforms, retaining omitted neck/attachment fields. Static mix accepts an optional bind pose; omitted fields in both clips stay omitted.

apis.name: AnimationTimeline
apis.signature: new AnimationTimeline({ durationMs, tracks, clock?, events? }); seek/play/pause/tick/step
constraints: Time is milliseconds. A shared injected clock drives every track. prepare may decode asynchronously; commit must be synchronous and non-throwing, release reclaims staged values.
All preparations must succeed before committing. Latest request wins; pause and dispose invalidate in-flight work. Seek does not replay historical events. Property ownership conflicts are rejected.
Adapters must snapshot decoded color/matte pixels during prepare; do not commit live video aliases that can be changed by superseded decoders.

apis.name: importFigmaMotion
constraints: First version recognizes explicit flamo.figma-motion-exchange v1, not arbitrary Dev Mode or plugin JSON. No native motion data yields NO_MOTION; unrecognized schemas yield UNKNOWN_FORMAT.
Supports numeric x/y/width/height/rotation/opacity/scaleX/scaleY, linear/hold/cubic-bezier and shared once/loop/boomerang cohorts. Absolute values retain source offsets.

Springs, paths and unsupported properties fail closed; never approximate physical springs as Bezier or silently drop tracks. Bind each source node id to a verified project node before applying samples.

apis.name: ctx.onUpdate
constraints: deltaTime is seconds; callback and unsubscribe belong to the script scope.

apis.name: defineNodeScript
constraints: New Node Script source uses the Vue 3 parameter order setup(props, ctx); props is the first argument and Runtime capabilities are on ctx.
props is one shallow-readonly reactive proxy for the current concrete instance public surface. Read props inside handlers or watch getters and write only through ctx.instance.setProps().
Ordinary Components, inherited Component Set scripts, and ordinary graphic nodes all use setup(props, ctx). The target changes the source of props, not the setup signature.
An inherited Component Set script reads the current instance selection and imported component properties, never the owning page or definition root props; separate instances remain isolated.

For an ordinary graphic node, props contains owning FlamoInstance inputs plus Node Script overlay props; x, y, size, fill, opacity, text, and other node visual fields are not projected into props. Use ctx.node(), ctx.$/ctx.$$, or ctx.scene queries with design/current snapshots and semantic setters or animations.
defineNodeScript<Props> is TypeScript typing only and does not create an Artifact public surface. Promote externally configurable persistent values to a component boundary with a canonical surface.
update, variantchange, componentpropertychange, and reload synchronize the same props proxy so ctx.watch(() => props.name, ...) observes committed changes.

ctx.props is a deprecated alias retained for compiled setup(ctx) compatibility. New TypeScript declarations require setup(props, ctx); getVariant/getComponentProperties remain advanced introspection APIs.

apis.name: ctx.on
apis.signature: ctx.on(eventName, (event: NodeScriptEventMap[eventName]) => void, { capture?, once?, passive? }?)
constraints: Consumes canonical Runtime input only; public ctx.emit output is not looped back into ctx.on.
Events route on the canonical ECS ancestry path in capture, target, and bubble phases; stopPropagation, stopImmediatePropagation, preventDefault, once, and passive follow DOM-style semantics.
Pointer and click coordinates are under event.coordinates, never event.position.
event.coordinates.local is relative to the event target. Use ctx.eventPoint(event, targetRef) for a child role or another node.
Common routed families include pointer, click, wheel, focus, keyboard, drag, tap/pan/pinch/rotate, input/composition, and clipboard events.

Runtime owns hit-testing: the Web path uses dirty-on-change color-ID picking with event-time pixel reads, while unsupported or Canvas2D paths use the same interaction descriptors for affine and clip-aware CPU fallback.
Use pointerdown rather than click when an internal pointer transaction must be marked before a DOM input blur.

apis.name: NodeScriptEvent
apis.signature: NodeScriptEvent<T> = T with target: string | null, currentTarget: string | null, composedPath(): string[]
constraints: target is the canonical Runtime ECS id selected by framework-owned hit-testing; its logical identity remains stable across Variant rematerialization for the complete pointer transaction.
currentTarget and phase update as the event traverses capture, target, and bubble listeners.
composedPath() returns a defensive copy of the canonical target-to-instance-root ECS id chain, including dynamically materialized component descendants.
User scripts must not reconstruct the target chain from bounds, colors, clone ids, or private ECS parent fields.

apis.name: NodeScriptEventMap
constraints: This is the complete typed routed event set for the current semantic-v1 Runtime manifest.
Pointer capture, focus, gesture, input, composition, and clipboard families use the same canonical target chain and listener options as pointer and click events.
HTML Surface input, composition, and clipboard events are bridged into the same NodeScriptEvent target projection.

apis.name: ctx.eventPoint
constraints: Converts event.coordinates.world through the target node's live world transform.
Prefer this over hard-coded parent offsets or design-time transform arithmetic.
Returns null if the target cannot be probed or its transform is singular.

apis.name: ctx.mounted
constraints: This is the explicit read boundary for the current physical ECS materialization; SceneApi remains semantic-only.
resolve returns the canonical mounted entity plus semanticRef, sourceNodeId, instanceRootId, live probe, and scene revision when available.
children returns current direct mounted children in ECS relation order; it does not perform recursive name lookup.
Mounted entity handles are transient across Variant replacement, slot replacement, and rematerialization. Re-resolve after revision changes and never persist or parse physical ids.

apis.name: ctx.mountedContent
apis.signature: ctx.mountedContent(viewportRoleOrNodeRef) -> { viewport, contents, primary, viewportSnapshot, contentSnapshots, primarySnapshot, revision } | null
constraints: Deprecated compatibility projection of ctx.mounted.children(viewportRoleOrNodeRef); new scripts should use ctx.mounted.
Returns current physical direct children without requiring physical clone-id parsing in the script.
Use revision to invalidate cached scroll geometry after slot replacement or scene mutation.
Measure during mount or revision change, not inside every pointermove.

apis.name: ctx.createShapeBatch
apis.signature: ctx.createShapeBatch({ node, polygon, capacity }) -> { update(Float32Array, count), dispose() }
constraints: Owner must already be mounted; polygon is a flat finite simple polygon [x,y,...]. Capacity is 1..100000.
Each instance contains [m00,m10,m01,m11,m02,m12,r,g,b,a] in owner-local coordinates. RGBA is 0..1. Frame data is validated and copied atomically.
Copies inherit owner and ancestor transform, opacity, visibility, render order and clipping. They are ephemeral, non-interactive and do not create individual scene nodes.
One WebGPU/WebGL2 instanced draw per batch; update count 0 hides all copies. Dispose is idempotent and automatic on script teardown.
Use separate batches for separate materials; do not persist physical owner IDs or GPU state in Artifact.

apis.name: ctx.createShaderLayer
apis.signature: ctx.createShaderLayer({ wgsl, glsl, label?, uniforms?, phase? }) -> ShaderLayerHandle
constraints: Managed screen-space GPU fragment layer, independent of the scene camera; background before native nodes or foreground after them.
Supply fn flamoFragment(uv: vec2<f32>) -> vec4<f32> in WGSL and vec4 flamoFragment(vec2 uv) in GLSL. UV origin is top-left; output straight-alpha RGBA. Engine entry points and bindings are reserved.
WGSL built-ins: flamo.resolution, flamo.time, flamo.parameters[0..3] (vec4). GLSL built-ins: u_resolution, u_time, u_parameters[0..3]. Up to 16 finite float uniforms and 8 layers per canvas.

Handle provides ready, status, error, setUniforms(values), setTime(seconds|null), setVisible(visible), dispose(). Compile errors reject ready and leave the native scene running. Script disposal automatically releases GPU resources.
The layer fills the canvas and does not inherit node fills, visibility or clipping. Make opaque native background fills transparent when composing a shader behind them.

apis.name: ctx.setTransformsBatch
apis.signature: ctx.setTransformsBatch([{ ref, x, y }, ...]) -> { accepted, missing }
constraints: Queues every accepted position write on the owning SceneRuntime fast channel.
Use one batch per scheduled frame for content and thumb motion.
The fast-channel flush publishes one scene mutation revision for the batch so renderer and picking refresh from one committed geometry state.

apis.name: ctx.onNode
apis.signature: ctx.onNode(roleOrNodeRef, eventName, (event: NodeScriptEventMap[eventName]) => void, { capture?, once?, passive? }?)
constraints: Binds directly to the role or node that participates in hit-testing instead of depending on parent bubbling.
Prefer role names from nodeArtifacts[*].roles, such as ctx.onNode('body', 'pointerdown', handler).
Common roles are inferred only from unambiguous component child names; Runtime selector fallback is a compatibility path and emits a persistence warning.
Use ctx.eventPoint(event, targetRef) when coordinates are needed in another role's local space.

apis.name: ctx.delegate
apis.signature: ctx.delegate(eventName, { name, scope? }, (event: NodeScriptEventMap[eventName]) => void, { capture?, once?, passive? }?)
constraints: Matches an exact node name against the framework-owned canonical event target path; scope defaults to the current script boundary.
The query is resolved when each event occurs so variant changes and dynamically present or absent nodes require no user-script cache.
Use this instead of geometry, bounds, pick colors, clone-id parsing, or manual parent traversal in user scripts.
No match is a normal no-op, including when the dynamic node does not currently exist.
pointerenter, pointerleave, focus, blur, and pointer-capture boundary events do not bubble; Runtime emits a development diagnostic and delegates them through the stable ancestor capture path.

apis.name: ctx.onChild
apis.signature: ctx.onChild(eventName, { name, scope? }, handler, { capture?, once?, passive? }?)
constraints: Binds directly to every current exact-name descendant, including non-bubbling boundary events.
Bindings are refreshed after Variant, component-property, and Artifact rematerialization.
Use this for dynamic descendants whose physical clone ids may change.

apis.name: ctx.onActivate
constraints: Unifies pointer click and non-repeating Enter or Space keyboard activation.
The same disabled rule gates every input modality.
Keyboard activation prevents the platform default unless preventDefault is false.

apis.name: RuntimeNode.on
apis.signature: runtimeNode.on(event: UnifiedEventType, handler: UnifiedEventHandler, { capture?, once?, passive? }?) -> dispose
constraints: Registers a lifecycle-owned listener directly on a live Runtime node and returns an idempotent disposer.
Uses the same canonical ECS target chain, event payloads, Interact policy, and listener semantics as ctx.on and ctx.onNode.
Prefer ctx.delegate for dynamically present named descendants so variant changes do not require rebinding.

apis.name: ctx.emit
constraints: Emits one public component business event such as onClose or onClick through the current Flamo instance; consumers receive the payload directly.
Use routed input listeners to decide when to emit; ctx.emit does not replace framework hit-testing or input propagation.
Internal Node Script messaging uses ctx.bus.emit/on instead of ctx.emit/on.
Public event names must be static string literals so the build can persist them in the canonical Artifact surface.
Keep the payload serializable when the event crosses host or Web Component boundaries.

apis.name: ctx.expose
constraints: Exposes public component methods; internal helpers remain ordinary module or closure functions.
Method names must be static object keys so the build can persist imperative ABI in the canonical Artifact surface.
Legacy non-boundary expose remains Runtime-compatible for one migration window but emits a deprecation diagnostic.

apis.name: ctx.bus
apis.signature: ctx.bus.on(eventName, handler) -> dispose; ctx.bus.emit(eventName, payload?) -> void
constraints: Provides transient internal messaging scoped to one FlamoRuntime; separate Runtime instances never share events.
Subscriptions are owned by the current Node Script scope and are removed automatically on dispose.
One throwing or rejecting subscriber is diagnosed without preventing later subscribers from running.
Bus events do not enter the Artifact surface, host CustomEvent channel, or canonical input router.

apis.name: ctx.components.create
apis.signature: await ctx.components.create(exportNameOrExactRef, { parent?, props?, placement?, key?, signal? }?) -> ComponentInstanceHandle
constraints: A string resolves one export and its complete definition closure from the owning Artifact.
An exact ref is resolved through the configured FlamoComponentResolver and must pass Artifact revision, hashes, Runtime ABI, and component ABI checks.
Creation is parent-owned, cancellable, and rolled back without a half-mounted entity on failure; one owner may retain at most 1000 dynamic child instances.
placement supports append, prepend, before, and after; before/after may specify a local gap.

apis.name: ctx.components.createBatch
constraints: One batch accepts at most 100 requests and may be cancelled with a shared AbortSignal; an individual request signal takes precedence.
If one request fails, every instance created earlier in the batch is destroyed in reverse order.

apis.name: ComponentInstanceHandle
apis.signature: { readonly id, readonly root, setProps(patch, { signal? }?), on(event, handler), inspect(), destroy() }
constraints: The handle belongs to one live child instance; on returns an idempotent disposer and destroy is idempotent.
setProps uses the same serialized atomic property transaction as FlamoInstance.setProps.
inspect exposes public state together with current ownership and cleanup counters.

apis.name: ctx.self.destroy
constraints: Idempotently destroys the whole owning FlamoInstance; self does not mean the current ctx.nodeId when a Component or Component Set script is inherited inside a page Runtime.
Never use this API to remove the current mounted node; use ctx.scene.remove(ctx.nodeId) or RuntimeNode.remove() instead.
Downloaded-project verification rejects ctx.self.destroy() in reusable Node Scripts; whole-Runtime teardown belongs to the host through instance.destroy().
Parent-owned descendants, listeners, scheduled tasks, surfaces, captures, and resource references are disposed recursively.

apis.name: instance.setProps
constraints: Validates the complete patch before commit and serializes property mutations per instance.
Variant changes complete before non-Variant bindings and public update events become observable.
A failed or cancelled Variant batch restores the prior selections and does not publish a partial props state.

Inside a Node Script inherited by a concrete Component Set instance, ctx.instance.setProps resolves against the effective inherited surface and automatically targets that instance rather than the owning page Artifact.
Unknown, unbound, or out-of-scope properties are rejected; a scoped Variant-axis commit includes an applied receipt for the concrete instance in variantReceipts.

apis.name: instance.inspect
constraints: The lifecycle snapshot includes descendant ownership, Node Script disposers, routed listeners, pending tasks and mutations, slot surfaces, resource references, ECS entity count, and limbo component count.
Use the snapshot before and after destroy-oriented tests to verify that owned resources return to zero without reading private Runtime fields.

apis.name: ctx.behavior
constraints: Select multi-behavior nodes by exact behaviorRef@version identity, for example ctx.behavior('select.behavior@1.0.0').
role(name) requires exactly one bound target; collection roles must use roles(name).
Role targets are mapped into the current component instance scope before handles are returned.
Missing, duplicate, or ambiguous bindings and unresolved role targets fail closed with contract.* interaction trace diagnostics.
ctx.role(name) remains the compatibility API for nodeArtifacts[*].roles; Behavior implementations should consume nodeArtifacts[*].interactions[].roleBindings through ctx.behavior().

apis.name: ctx.trace
constraints: Use structured action names and include viewport policy, caret index, and scroll offset for complex interactions.
Local preview retains the latest 500 trace entries for window.__flamo_project.traceInteraction().

apis.name: flamo.registerProxyBinding
constraints: Call flamo.unregisterProxyBinding(nodeId) immediately before hot-registering the same node.
The binding callback must always return an object, even for lifecycle-only scripts.
Use hooks.useReactive for state, hooks.useEntityProxy for ECS writes, hooks.onMounted/onUnmounted for external listeners.
For mounted Flamo instances, pass a scoped API from instance.createScopedFlamoApi(...) and register against flamo.resolveNodeId(reference) so source IDs map to the current instance.

apis.name: instance.createScopedFlamoApi
constraints: Use this before activating an interaction script for a mounted Flamo instance.
The scoped API maps original node IDs, local IDs, and selectors such as '#Content' to that instance's runtime nodes.
Do not store a single global disposer for all activations; key cleanup by flamo.instance.id or by the scoped root node.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).animate
apis.signature: handle.animate({ x?, y?, width?, height?, scaleX?, scaleY?, rotation?, 'NodeCpt.opacity'? }, { duration, easing })
constraints: Use 'NodeCpt.opacity' for whole-node opacity; bare opacity is invalid in EntityHandle animate/set/get.
Do not use bare scale.
Prefer scaleX/scaleY, handle.setScale(), or handle.animateScale() for reliable visual scaling across node types.
width/height mutate TransformCpt.size and may trigger node-type-specific geometry rebuild semantics.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).animateScale
constraints: Use this for visual scaling when the intent is to scale what the user sees rather than redefining semantic width/height.
This API maps to TransformCpt.transform.m00/m11.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).setText
constraints: Use this for dynamic text instead of setting TextCpt.textData directly in generated scripts.
The runtime clears TextCpt.derivedTextData so stale Figma baselines cannot clip the new string.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).design
constraints: Preferred read API for identity, hierarchy, geometry, compositing, layout, constraints, appearance, text, media, interaction, component, HTML surface, canvas, and accessibility semantics.
Returns a normalized design-time snapshot; defaults and lossy conversions are reported in warnings.
Do not parse private Figma guid, derived text, geometry cache, or instance override encodings in ordinary scripts.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).current
constraints: Waits for queued writes and merges live probe geometry, visibility, and opacity with normalized design semantics.
Use this instead of handle.get() when verifying a post-mutation runtime result.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).measureText
constraints: Uses normalized font family, style, weight, size, and letter spacing from the text semantic snapshot.
Prefer this over manually constructing a Canvas font from raw Figma fields.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).semanticWrites
constraints: Prefer intent APIs over guessed ECS property paths.
Check semantic-properties.manifest.json for applicability and read/write support.

apis.name: flamo.createEntityHandle(nodeId).setInteractive
apis.signature: handle.setInteractive({ mode?: 'auto' | 'enabled' | 'disabled', enabled?, pointerEvents?: 'auto' | 'none' | 'box-only' | 'box-none', inert?, hitTestWhenTransparent?, cursor?, zIndex? })
constraints: mode disabled and inert are authoritative and cannot be overridden by registered listeners.
mode auto activates an interaction boundary only when it has routed listeners; enabled keeps the boundary active without listeners.
pointerEvents none rejects the subtree, box-only rejects descendants, and box-none excludes only the node's own pick surface.
hitTestWhenTransparent preserves an explicit hit surface at paint opacity zero while visible=false still removes it from interaction.
enabled is a compatibility projection; prefer mode for new code.

apis.name: app.playMotion
apis.signature: app.playMotion({ name, driver, duration, tracks: [{ target, channel, sampler, keyframes }], budget })
constraints: MotionSpec channel: 'opacity' is allowed.
Use multiple keyframed tracks for concrete performance motion such as arc throws.

apis.name: handle.layout
constraints: Returns parent participation, per-axis property owners and local border/content boxes. Inspect source: design is not live measurement.
Node Script geometry writes reject layout-owned axes before command submission, including set, animate and fast setters. Layout/constraint edits belong to explicit scene authoring.
Use setHeight or setWidth for a single fixed input axis; setSize may also overwrite a layout-owned dimension.

apis.name: handle.setHeight
constraints: Finite non-negative input height only. Does not rewrite width or position.

apis.name: handle.setWidth
constraints: Finite non-negative input width only. Does not rewrite height or position.

apis.name: ctx.observeLayout
apis.signature: ctx.observeLayout(ref: string | EntityHandle, callback: (layout: NodeLayoutSnapshot | null) => void): () => void
constraints: Immediately reports current layout/null, then changed snapshots of the latest committed layout.
Subscriptions share a script-owned Runtime sampler, execute in the owning SceneRuntime and dispose with the script. Static layout() reads alone are not reactive subscriptions.

apis.name: ctx.assertLayoutWritable
apis.signature: ctx.assertLayoutWritable(ref: string | EntityHandle, properties: readonly string[]): void
constraints: Preflight only: validates all requested layout-sensitive property paths before writes. Unavailable targets and layout conflicts throw.
Setters and ctx mutation paths still enforce ownership; callers cannot disable protection by skipping preflight.

apis.name: ctx.instance.app.getResourcePool
constraints: Borrow the host device and registry. Do not create a second device or destroy the pool.

apis.name: ctx.createGpuSurface
constraints: Experimental WebGPU only. Explicit ready/render/resize and scope-owned dispose; nearest or linear integer output scale.
Public declarations are emitted from runtime/src/3d and delivered with the exact runtime-contract bundle hash.
Use surface.own(resource) to transfer disposal. Never transfer the shared device or externally borrowed buffers.
